name: Small-strain high-shear-stiffness cantilever bending, ten elements

source.originalStudy: Prathap and Bhashyam (1982), International Journal for Numerical Methods in Engineering, volume 18, pages 195–210

case.model: straight cantilever, clamped at x=0, transverse tip load in local y

limitations: The MOOSE reference case uses an Euler-Bernoulli beam; OmniEng evaluates its Timoshenko element with the published high-shear-stiffness properties. This tests the thin-beam limit and does not add an Euler-Bernoulli element formulation.
The public beam module exposes an element stiffness matrix, not a beam-mesh assembler. The verification harness assembles the documented straight, uniform mesh and uses the production sparse solver.
The source load is scaled by 1e-4 relative to the cited study; the fixture preserves the MOOSE V&V input scaling and its reported ten-element result.
This is an experimental cross-solver correlation for one linear beam case. It does not establish mesh convergence, general beam workflow validation, or release maturity.
Redistribution rights for the source documentation/data have not been independently reviewed.
